notes:
Summary: Brickford builds a cloud-based contact center layer used by mid-market retailers. Evaluating Redwood for real-time agent assist + ticket summarization. Primary ask: streaming low-latency suggestions, safe tool-calling hooks (CRM update + escalation), and reliability under promotional spikes.

Key requirements / customer language: 
- "Low-latency streaming" p95 < 200ms for suggestion tokens, aim p99 < 350ms under steady load.
- Support 200 concurrent live agents with headroom to burst to ~1200 for holiday/promotions.
- Guardrails: hallucination filters, immediate content moderation, deterministic tool-call confirmation flow.
- Prefer open-model variants (quantized Llama-family) for cost; want automatic fallback to stronger closed model for complex policy language.
- Must support VPC deployment or on-prem appliance for specific retail customers; data residency for EU customers.
- Integration touchpoints: CRM webhooks, internal ticket system (Jira), SSO via Okta.

POC scope: 4 weeks, start w/ 50 agents, measure latency/throughput, evaluate batching/caching gains via Redwood Optimize suggestions. Success metrics agreed: suggestion accuracy > 85% on golden prompt set; median suggestion latency < 120ms; <1% failure rate on tool-call executions.

Quotes / call snippets: "We need the model to behave like an assistant that never invents policy steps — if unsure, suggest escalation." AE notes: customer is cost-conscious but willing to pay for predictable SLAs.

Technical asks to track: KV/prefix cache behavior for repeated ticket patterns; token-level cost breakdown in Console; ability to pin model versions for rollouts; can Redwood enforce per-customer response retention controls?
